transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really restless. Like I can’t quite settle in my own body, especially when I’m supposed to sit still and do paperwork or talk through household plans. It’s been getting hard to manage.
How long have you been experiencing this restlessness—has it been going on for years, or did it start more recently?
It’s been… more noticeable recently. Since I got married, really—when our routines kind of merged. So, about a year and five months ago.
Aside from the household and marriage-related situations, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things in your life, like work, health, or finances?
Um… I don’t think so. Not in a way that stands out to me. I mean, I think about normal things, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time about work or health or money.
Have you noticed any physical changes recently, like your heart racing, unexplained weight loss, excessive sweating, or feeling unusually hot or shaky?
Not really… I haven’t noticed anything like that. Nothing that feels unusual physically, I guess.
Have you noticed any trembling or shakiness in your hands, especially when trying to hold something steady?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed my hands shaking when I’m holding something.

Does this restlessness mainly happen when you're dealing with household or marriage-related tasks, or do you also feel it in situations completely unrelated to your marriage, like at work or during leisure time?

It’s mostly when I’m supposed to sit down and deal with household stuff… paperwork, plans we’re supposed to make together, that kind of thing. I just feel like I can’t really settle in my own body. I guess I notice it most there.
Would you say this restlessness has started to interfere with your daily activities, work, or your relationship with your spouse?

Yeah… I think it has. Mostly at home, and with some volunteer things. People can’t really count on me the way they should, because I keep dropping things or not following through, even when I’m trying. I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because of it.
When you get a break from those household or marriage-related tasks—like on a vacation or a day without those responsibilities—does the restlessness go away, or does it still linger?

It eases some if I’m not facing that stuff, I guess. But it doesn’t totally go away. The worst of it is when I’m supposed to sit still and deal with paperwork or household plans… that’s when I really feel like I can’t settle in my own body.
When you start to feel this restlessness or unease, do you find it hard to control or stop those anxious feelings, even in moments unrelated to household or marriage tasks?
I’m not really sure. I notice it most with those household things, so it’s hard to separate out. In other moments… maybe a little, but I haven’t paid that much attention to it.
Before you got married and your routines merged, had you ever experienced this kind of restlessness or unease, even briefly, in other areas of your life?

Maybe a little, but it’s hard for me to remember clearly. What I’m noticing now is more that I just… can’t settle in my own body, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or household plans. Before marriage, I don’t know if I would’ve described it the same way.

Do you feel like this restlessness and unease is directly connected to adjusting to married life and merging routines with your spouse, or does it feel more like a general anxiousness that exists on its own, separate from that specific change in your life?

I don’t know if I’d call it general anxiousness exactly. It feels more like… I just can’t settle in my body, especially when I’m supposed to sit still and deal with paperwork or the shared household plans. So it’s tied to that, at least that’s when I notice it most.
Since these feelings started around your marriage, have you also been feeling unusually sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually sad or stopped caring about things.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels since these feelings started?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed anything major with sleep or appetite. Energy… I mean, it varies, but nothing that feels like a clear change.
Sorry, I’m not sure I caught the question. Could you ask it again?
Do you feel like your level of distress or difficulty coping with these household and marriage-related changes is more intense than what most people might experience in a similar situation?

I guess… yes, maybe more than I’d like to admit. It’s gotten to where people at home and in my volunteer stuff can’t really count on me the way they used to. I’ve had to step back from some things because I keep letting things fall through, even when I’m trying.
